basis.vllm: per-kernel decode profile at the binding baseline identity, this issue (tables/bs*_kernels.csv)
basis.mpk: integrated-HEAD (c80ebd68) LATE-CONTEXT capture, msl=897 = 256-token synthetic prompt + 640 decode steps + 1, mbt=16, page_size=256, gate_padding_rows ON, attn_q_pass=2, no admission cap at bs1/8 (bs16 uncapped for this capture) -- opt/m3i7/stage/armL/pertask_by_bs.csv. SUPERSEDES the M3-I10 matched-geometry (msl=353) capture this file used before, for a structural reason and not just freshness: at msl=353 the exact admission replay has NO prefill-free regime wider than FIVE live requests at bs8 or bs16 (the first request retires at iteration 112, the last finishes prefilling at 128 / 256), so that geometry cannot express a bs8 or bs16 decode step at all -- and the committed armA capture in fact fell through parse_profile's `hi <= lo` guard into the last-eight-iterations fallback, recording regime (1 live, 0 prefill, 1 decode, 1 token) and tokens_per_step=1 for both. msl=897 yields a genuine full-width 8-live decode step at bs8 ([170,656), 486 iterations) and 12/16 at bs16 ([720,733)), and it samples the decode-context band the vLLM reference table was itself captured at (556-896) -- the argument M3-I10 already accepted for the attention row, applied here to every stage. Window alignment: parse_profile's window is centred on concurrency.py's own midpoint iteration per bs (opt/m3i7/scripts/window_plan.py, which prints the regime enumeration it derives that from), so the per-stage wall spans and the step_us they are normalised against come from the same iterations. Anchor-QC (per-step task-type counts vs the compiled task graph) run per bs before publication.
basis.target_rule: beat the corresponding vLLM kernel by 25 % => target = 0.75x the vLLM number
basis.rank_rule: targets ranked by NEW step_gain_if_met_us at bs1, descending (comparison_by_stage.csv carries no rank column; this is the one place this file imposes an ordering choice, stated here so it is reproducible).
basis.caveat: Two caveats, both structural rather than fixable by re-running. (1) bs16 still has no full-width prefill-free window at ANY context -- staggered admission means the 16 requests never all decode simultaneously, so its step is measured over the widest available regime (12 of 16 live, 13 iterations, per-slot contexts spread across ~263-890). Read bs16 as directionally right, not as precise as bs1/bs8. bs1 (1 live, the whole 640-step decode) and bs8 (8 live, 486 iterations) are clean. (2) The MPK column is one step from one profiled rep per bs; the wave wall it sits inside was measured over three unprofiled reps with a full range of 0.02-3.3% (opt/m3i7/tables/), and per-step task-event counts are schedule-determined, so a single profiled rep is sufficient for the decomposition but the ABSOLUTE step is still a single-rep number. Stage ratios, which are what the targets are ranked on, are ratios inside one capture and are insensitive to that.

_summary.meaning: anchor QC compares the per-step task-type counts the trace implies against the counts the compiled task graph contains; a window that fails is not a step at the stated batch size. Rows for a FAILing bs are retained for continuity and flagged, not used for ranking (the rank is computed on bs1).

dispositions.reason: RESOLVED by M3-I2b's quantize-redundancy fix, confirmed at matched geometry / current HEAD (anchor-QC exact, max_frac_err=0.0000 at every bs). Wallspan collapsed 4540->533.0 us/step at bs1 (ratio 8.12x->1.00x); code-delta isolation (committed M3-I1 vs this remeasure's arm B, SAME msl=132 geometry, current HEAD) attributes the full move to the code change -- geometry delta (arm B -> arm A) on top of that is negligible (562->560 us/step at bs1). No ferret dispatch: there is nothing left to buy. See opt/m3i10/remeasure/ (pertask_by_bs.csv code-delta columns) for the arm-B-vs-M3-I1 isolation.

MPK is 4.3-8.5x slower, but the whole stage is 28-102 us/step against a 15.3-22.0 ms MPK step, i.e. 0.19-0.46 %. A ferret run cannot pay for itself here. Worth re-checking if MPK's step ever drops below ~5 ms, where the bs16 gap would be ~2 %. The ratio grows with batch (4.26 -> 7.86 -> 8.54) because MPK's 128 argmax_partial tasks each scan ~1940 vocab rows and their mean cost scales with batch (5.38 -> 61.68 us/task), while vLLM's single reduce kernel goes 8.68 -> 13.47 us.

MPK runs the whole embedding gather as ONE task at concurrency 1.0 (52.0 us mean for a single-token lookup at bs1, vs vLLM's 2.47 us). The 6-22x ratio is graph WIDTH, not kernel quality: there is nothing for a ferret kernel to make faster, because one CTA is doing a memcpy-shaped job. The fix is a builder change (split the embedding across workers), and it belongs with M3-I1 backlog rank 3 'widen the narrow task stages', not in a kernel dispatch. Absolute gap is 42-52 us/step (0.2-0.3 % of the step) either way.

MPK is only 1.20-1.27x behind and the absolute gap is 38-49 us/step (0.2-0.3 % of the step) at every batch size. Beating vLLM by 20-30 % here recovers under 50 us. Re-rank only if the stages above it are closed.
